A price that big also says something about **Fiserv (****FISV:NASDAQ****)**, whose Clover competes for the same merchants, and **PayPal (****PYPL:NASDAQ****)**, which chases the same merchants through Braintree.

It's happened before: the stock jumped 11% on Oct. 30 on a $40 billion buyout report, then sank 12% on Nov. 12 when GTCR and Clayton, Dubilier & Rice walked away.

The third quarter backed that up: adjusted EPS rose 10% to $3.58, and management reaffirmed its 2026 outlook.

At today's price it's around 6x. That isn't much of a takeover premium for earnings expected to grow by double digits a year.

Fiserv and PayPal are cheap too. Fiserv trades at 7.4x, and its Merchant Solutions organic revenue fell 2% in the third quarter. Would a debt-heavy, private Global Payments fight harder on price for merchants, or spend less competing with Clover?

PayPal, at 9.6x, named Xero's Claire Bramley its next CFO today, a sign management wants to fix the business in public.

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Global Payments, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Global Payments' Analyst Ratings

Debt rose from $17.0 billion in 2024 to $22.2 billion in 2025, so a big chunk of any $50 billion price would go to refinancing it. GTCR is reportedly lining up other firms to share the financing this time.

I'd own Global Payments at around 6x earnings, deal or no deal. But today's gain could vanish as fast as October's did. Fourth-quarter results, due early next year, need to keep normalized revenue growth above 4%.
